scenes.tts: A hawk's shadow slides across a meadow. What does a mouse's optic nerve tell its brain about it?
scenes.visual: A meadow under a pale sky; a hawk-shaped shadow glides across the grass. Beside it, a mouse eye with the optic nerve leaving the back. Question on screen: what does the optic nerve tell the brain?
scenes.narration: A hawk's shadow slides across a meadow. What does a mouse's optic nerve tell its brain about it?

scenes.tts: Every signal the brain receives from the eye leaves through ganglion cells.
scenes.visual: Cross-section of the retina. The innermost layer of ganglion cells glows gold; their axons run along the inner surface and gather into the optic nerve.
scenes.narration: Every signal the brain receives from the eye leaves through ganglion cells.

scenes.tts: They are the retina's only output neurons, and their axons make the optic nerve.
scenes.visual: Label: ganglion cells = the retina's only output. The axon bundle is labelled optic nerve.
scenes.narration: They are the retina's only output neurons, and their axons make the optic nerve.

scenes.tts: So does that nerve carry a picture, like a camera cable?
scenes.visual: A camera cable drawn beside the optic nerve, with a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: So does that nerve carry a picture, like a camera cable?

scenes.tts: It does not. A mouse has more than forty types of ganglion cell.
scenes.caption: It does not. A mouse has more than 40 types of ganglion cell.
scenes.visual: The camera cable fades. Text on screen: more than 40 types of ganglion cell (mouse).
scenes.narration: It does not. A mouse has more than 40 types of ganglion cell.

scenes.tts: Each type reports the scene through its own filter.
scenes.visual: The meadow scene passes through several differently tinted lenses, each giving a different version of the same scene.
scenes.narration: Each type reports the scene through its own filter.

scenes.tts: Some filters are simple. They signal local differences in brightness.
scenes.visual: One version shows only patches where brightness differs locally, as bright and dark blotches.
scenes.narration: Some filters are simple. They signal local differences in brightness.

scenes.tts: Others are highly selective. They detect a small object moving, or motion in one direction.
scenes.visual: A second version shows only the small moving shadow lit up; a third shows an arrow for one direction of motion.
scenes.narration: Others are highly selective. They detect a small object moving, or motion in one direction.

scenes.tts: Bipolar and amacrine circuits inside the retina build each filter, before any spike leaves the eye.
scenes.visual: Back to the retina cross-section: bipolar and amacrine cells light up between photoreceptors and ganglion cells. Text: filters built inside the retina.
scenes.narration: Bipolar and amacrine circuits inside the retina build each filter, before any spike leaves the eye.

scenes.tts: Now look down on the retina as a flat sheet, and light up one type.
scenes.visual: The retina flattens into a round sheet seen from above. Gold dots appear, spread across the whole sheet.
scenes.narration: Now look down on the retina as a flat sheet, and light up one type.

scenes.tts: Its cells spread across the retina. Each cell tends to keep some distance from its neighbours.
scenes.visual: Each gold dot keeps a gap from its nearest neighbours; short lines show the spacing is fairly even. Label: illustrative type.
scenes.narration: Its cells spread across the retina. Each cell tends to keep some distance from its neighbours.

scenes.tts: Their dendrites can overlap a lot, and spacing and arbor size vary across the retina.
scenes.visual: A translucent disc grows around each dot for its dendritic arbor; the discs overlap, and dots and discs grow a little larger toward one edge. Label: illustrative.
scenes.narration: Their dendrites can overlap a lot, and spacing and arbor size vary across the retina.

scenes.tts: That even spacing is called a mosaic. So one type draws one map of the scene.
scenes.visual: Label: mosaic. The gold sheet is labelled: one type = one map.
scenes.narration: That even spacing is called a mosaic. So one type draws one map of the scene.

scenes.tts: Lay a second type over the first. Then a third.
scenes.visual: A teal mosaic with its own spacing and arbor size is laid over the gold one, then a violet mosaic.
scenes.narration: Lay a second type over the first. Then a third.

scenes.tts: Predict. If each type draws one map, what does the optic nerve carry?
scenes.visual: The three stacked mosaics beside the optic nerve. Text: each type draws one map. So the nerve carries...?
scenes.narration: Predict. If each type draws one map, what does the optic nerve carry?

scenes.tts: More than forty overlapping maps of the scene, each filtered differently.
scenes.caption: More than 40 overlapping maps of the scene, each filtered differently.
scenes.visual: The optic nerve redrawn as a bundle of coloured strands, gold, teal, violet and many more. Text: more than 40 overlapping maps.
scenes.narration: More than 40 overlapping maps of the scene, each filtered differently.

scenes.tts: The brain can combine maps to build new features.
scenes.visual: Two strands merge into a new colour at a brain target.
scenes.narration: The brain can combine maps to build new features.

scenes.tts: But information that no map carries is gone before the brain has a chance.
scenes.visual: A part of the meadow scene that no strand carries greys out and drops away before the nerve.
scenes.narration: But information that no map carries is gone before the brain has a chance.

scenes.tts: The same idea suggests a check. If a type is really two, its spacing usually looks less regular.
scenes.visual: Two independently placed mosaics coloured alike so they look like one type; the spacing looks patchier, with some cells almost touching.
scenes.narration: The same idea suggests a check. If a type is really two, its spacing usually looks less regular.

scenes.tts: And more arbors cover each point than for comparable types. These are clues, not proof.
scenes.visual: Over the patchy group, a counter of arbors per point reads higher than for either mosaic alone. Label: a clue, not proof.
scenes.narration: And more arbors cover each point than for comparable types. These are clues, not proof.

scenes.tts: Hold one rule in mind. One type, one mosaic, one map.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: One type, one mosaic, one map. Three stacked mosaics feed a bundle of coloured strands.
scenes.narration: Hold one rule in mind. One type, one mosaic, one map.
